text: Imagine the situation. You have a girlfriend and everything seems to be fine. But she has this one female friend who doesn't like you. And because of that, from time to time, you get into some uncomfortable situations. This in a nutshell is a situation that happened to one of my subscribers. So here's the question that he sent me. Hello, I'm in a group chat with my girlfriend. There is mostly women. They all call me a green flag, but some of them call my girlfriend mine or baby girl. I have told my girlfriend that I don't really feel comfortable with them calling her that, as I'm scared to lose her, just as that it happens often in my relationship. There's this one particular girl. She's lesbian and supposed to have a girlfriend. Already, me and her do not get along very well. We often argue, but the rest of her friend groups loves her. She once even told me, get out of here, my name. My girlfriend did nothing. I do trust my girlfriend. She won't cheat, but I fear I might get out of control. And I have a strong feeling if I do tell that friend I'm not really comfortable with her calling my girlfriend that she will call me insecure, overreacting, etc. Yes, I have overreacted before, but we did reconcile. I just want to know if I should even like talk with that friend or even tell her I don't like it. So here was my answer. First of all, man, when you write a question, please use punctuation and take your time to structure it properly. It makes it much easier to read and understand. With that out of the way, first general point. What are you even doing in your girlfriend's girl's group chat? If these are not your friends, but her friends, let her have her own group chat. Same way you should have your own chat with your boys. Just doing this alone would probably save a lot of unnecessary headaches. Now about the other girls calling your girlfriend's baby girl or mine. Of course, context matters here, but unless you genuinely feel that someone is directly hitting on your girlfriend, this sounds relatively innocent. To me, it sounds like the kind of stuff girls say to each other, similar to how guys make gay jokes or call each other names in a boy's group chat. Now the first actually concerning point. There is a girl in that chat who told you to get out and who has conflicts with you. This is a red flag. If she openly tried to insult you and your girlfriend did nothing, that is bad. In a relationship, you two are one unit. Your girlfriend should step in and tell that friend to keep her mouth shut and never speak to you in that tone again. And if she can't respect that, then they shouldn't be friends. If I understood correctly, that girl is not your friend, but your girlfriend's friend. So your girlfriend is the one who should handle it. Bottom line, I don't see anything critically bad here overall. What you should do is talk to your girlfriend, explain how you feel, and then sit back and observe her reaction. If she understands you, sets boundaries with her friend, and makes it clear that disrespect towards you is not acceptable, that's a good sign and a green flag for the relationship. If she ignores it, dismisses you, refuses to compromise, or calls you insecure, then it's up to you. At that point, you either end the relationship, which actually would be my main suggestion, or treat this as a yellow card, meaning there's a high chance the relationship won't work long term and you should stay alert for any further red flags. Alright guys, hope this was an interesting question. My name is Ilyas Abdullin. Thanks a lot and bye.
